cards.text: A father is giving his son some serious advice, and friend, this is NOT a suggestion box. He opens with: "My son, keep my words and treasure my commandments within you."

cards.question: The father tells his son that keeping his commandments leads to life.

cards.text: He tells his son to guard his teachings as the apple of his eye. Then he names two places to keep them, and friend, this dad is covering EVERY base.

cards.question: Where does the father tell his son to tie his commandments and write them?

answers.text: On his fingers and his heart
On his doorposts and his gates
On a scroll and a stone tablet

cards.text: Then he tells his son to say to wisdom, "You are my sister," and to call understanding his kinsman. Wisdom's not some coworker you nod at in the elevator, friend, she's FAMILY.

cards.question: The father wants wisdom and understanding to be close so they may keep the son from the ___, the stranger with seductive words.

cards.text: Then the father tells what he saw, and every street's got one of these: the neighbor at the window who sees EVERYTHING. He says, "For at the window of my house I looked through the lattice."

cards.question: Watching through the lattice, the father notices among the simple youths a young man lacking ___.

cards.text: This young man is crossing the street near the adulteress's corner, strolling down the road to her house. Friend, he's not hurrying. He's STROLLING.

cards.question: When is the young man strolling down the road to the adulteress's house?

answers.text: At twilight as day fades to dark
At sunrise as the city wakes up
At noon in the heat of the day

cards.text: Then a woman comes out to meet the young man. She's wearing the attire of a harlot, and she's cunning of heart.

cards.question: The father describes this woman as quiet and happy to stay at home.

cards.text: She's loud and defiant, and her feet don't stay at home. Now in the street, now in the squares, she lurks at every corner.

cards.question: The woman walks right up to the young man. What does she do?

answers.text: She seizes him and kisses him

cards.text: Then she brazenly starts talking. She tells him she has made her peace offerings, and today she has paid her vows.

cards.question: The woman tells the young man she sought him and found him.

cards.text: Then she tells him she's decked her bed with colored linen from Egypt and perfumed it with myrrh, aloes and cinnamon.
Then she says, "Come, let us take our fill of love till morning…"

cards.question: The woman tells the young man her husband is at home.
The woman says her husband has gone on a long journey with a bag of money. When does she say he'll be back?

answers.text: Not till the moon is full
At the end of the week

cards.question: The woman gets the young man to go along with her through great persuasion and flattering ___.

cards.text: He follows her on impulse, like an ox going to the slaughter, like a deer bounding into a trap.

cards.question: An ox headed to the slaughter and a deer bounding into a trap. What do those pictures say about the young man?

answers.text: He's being chased by a hunter
He's strong enough to break free

cards.text: The father's pictures keep going, until an arrow pierces his liver, like a bird darting into a snare, not knowing it will cost him his life. This part is heavy, friend.
Now the father turns to his sons and tells them to listen to him and attend to the words of his mouth. Friend, this is the part of the meeting where NOBODY checks their email.

cards.question: What does the father tell his sons about the woman's ways?

answers.text: Do not let your heart turn aside to them
Go and see them once for yourself
Warn her husband when he returns

cards.question: The father says the woman has brought only a few people down.

cards.text: She has brought many down to death. Her slain are many in number.

cards.question: The father says the woman's house is the road to ___, descending to the chambers of death.
